### Historical audit — S0157

**Scope:** Only chunk 3 of 6 is visible. Citations below refer to `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/sceneevolve_cli/C2/test/commons_16007442/trajectory.jsonl` (S0157). The referenced images are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, JSONL line 20, chars [0,291709) | **Goal:** reconstruct an indoor scene from one RGB image as editable multipart SceneAct/Blender geometry, with matching camera and materials. The student described an electronics workbench; that description is an inferred scene interpretation, not independent image verification. |
| Student prior program and runner results embedded in line 20, chars [0,291709) | The program constructed multiple named assemblies: bench, walls, cabinets, monitor, oscilloscope, meters, lamp, keyboard, tools and cables. It used colored surfaces, roughness and screen emission, but no reference texture. Lamp arms, hinge and shade were grouped; meters and keyboard were rotated as assemblies. Grouping and coordinates do not independently establish physical connection or correct pose. |
| Student audit and revision embedded in line 20, chars [0,291709) | After step 1, the student *reported* reversed perspective, an exposed foreground gap, undersized monitor, high/thin lamp and washed-out lighting. It revised camera X, extended the desktop, enlarged the monitor, changed the lamp and reduced the main light. These are the student's visual judgments and executed code changes, not independently verified discrepancies or improvements. |
| Runner messages embedded in line 20, chars [0,291709) | Steps 1 and 2 each reported `ok: true`, completed 16 samples and saved a render and blend file. This establishes reported technical render success, not geometric or visual correctness. |
| Student `model_response`, line 22, chars [0,16110); `select`, line 23, chars [0,59); `execute`, line 24, chars [0,15913) | The student chose **BEST 2**, claimed better perspective and coverage, and proposed monitor rotation, a lower/longer lamp, larger meter, extended cables and darker materials. The nonempty full program was then submitted for step 3; the execute event confirms an attempt, **not its result**. The cable assembly was scaled separately from the meter, so whether its leads remain connected is an unresolved geometric question. |
| Student `codex_session`, line 21, chars [0,4762) | The session completed with zero tool calls; it was read-only, with shell, browser and image-viewing tools disabled. The supplied reference and prior renders were listed as model inputs. No teacher message, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption is visible in this chunk. |

**Outcome and lessons.** The visible record shows two reported successful renders and a third execution attempt; final submission, step 3 result and overall correctness are **unknown**. There is no visible empty patch, algorithm failure or technical interruption. Autonomous work consisted of image-based critique and code revision within the supplied constraints, not external exploration.

A transferable practice illustrated is separating suspected camera, local geometry and lighting causes before revising; its effectiveness here remains unverified. The specific camera reversal, monitor rotation and darkening are scene-specific hypotheses. Without the images or later events, actual object visibility, material fidelity, occlusion, connections, pose, lighting quality and whether step 3 improved the match cannot be determined.
